newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes sharply lower in jittery market.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes sharply lower in jittery market.

text.p: Precious metals prices were at low end of recent ranges on Monday at the start of a short holiday week featuring an over-the-counter options expiry and a possible U.S. interest rate hike, dealers said.
"Dealers are trying to position themselves ahead of the options expiry on Tuesday. It's also the end of the first quarter ahead of a long Easter weekend, so it's all happening," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $350.65 per ounce, compared with $352.80 on Friday afternoon. It came under fresh pressure in early Europe after sinking during Asian trading hours.
Bullion has been trading in a narrow band in recent days, and analysts said the market ahead of the expiry was focusing on $350 and $355 levels, the most popular strike prices.
"An OTC options expiry on Tuesday is likely to leave the gold market drifting for the next few days, and technically the market is neutral," brokers GNI said in a report.
However, a break below the psychological $350 level could signal further technical losses towards recent lows around $348 and then $345, traders noted.
Also at the forefront of the market's consciousness was Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which many dealers saw likely to raise interest rates by 25 basis points.
"There is no doubt in my mind that a hike of 25 basis points has been priced into the market. The question is whether it's going to be 25 or 50 basis points," a dealer said.
Silver prices were similarly shaky at $5.13/$5.15, down four cents from Friday's London close.
Prices were just a shade above important support at around $5.10 an ounce, below which the psychological $5.00 level would emerge as the next downside target.
The other white metals were also easier in the complex-wide weakness.
Platinum was $3.00 lower at $374.75/$375.75. Having fallen below the 30-day moving average around $376, platinum was vulnerable to further declines towards $370, dealers said.
Palladium was also sharply lower at $147.25/$148.25, down $4.75.
Both platinum group metals were still watching for fresh news on delayed Russian supply contract talks with Japan and planned strikes at the Russian Norilsk complex.
